bundle: WI-10 / L-035 — review record for the four nil declarations Work Item 3 made without a binding
reviewedBy: WI-10 (L-035) investigation — investment research review, acting under the owner assignment recorded in register 17.2 ("ingestion grammar (D-2 lineage) with investment research review")
whatThisIs: The second branch of the resolution L-035 names: "a review step that records who accepted the mapping". The first branch — a declaration grammar that binds a nil to a statement section and a line-item class — is implemented and tested in the same work item; this record applies it, after the fact, to the four declarations Work Item 3 made before the grammar existed. No Work Item 3 file is altered: this record cites it.

declarations.quotedWording: The Group has no outstanding borrowings.
declarations.locator: Note 2.11 FINANCIAL INSTRUMENTS -> Financial risk management -> Liquidity risk (document pages 20-26; parse chunk 13 of 17)
declarations.wi3DirectOrDerived: DIRECT at group level — the sentence is the filer's own statement about borrowings as a whole. Applying it to this individual component is a MAPPING decision (a component of a class the filer says is empty), recorded here rather than hidden in arithmetic.
declarations.acceptance: Accepted without qualification. The sentence is the group's own statement about borrowings as a whole; the component is a member of the class the group says is empty. Class matches (BORROWINGS), section matches (the balance sheet is where a borrowing would be presented), scope matches (both are the group). This is the mapping the old grammar could not distinguish from an arbitrary one — it is correct, and now it is checkable.

declarations.quotedWording: The Company has only one class of shares referred to as equity shares having a par value of ₹5/-.
declarations.locator: Note 2.12 EQUITY -> EQUITY SHARE CAPITAL (document pages 26-31; parse chunk 14 of 17)
declarations.wi3DirectOrDerived: DIRECT as a statement of share classes (parent Company); applied to the consolidated capital block by mapping — see scopeNuance

binding.acknowledgedBy: WI-10 L-035 review 2026-11-07 (originally mapped by WI-3)

declarations.acceptance: Accepted WITH a recorded scope nuance. The sentence speaks of "the Company" — the parent — and is applied to the consolidated capital block. Under the new grammar this mapping is legal only with an explicit acceptedBy, and this is that acceptance: consolidated owners' equity comprises only equity share capital and other equity, non-controlling interests are presented separately, and no preference instrument appears in the consolidated balance sheet or in the authorised share capital. The class (PREFERENCE_SHARE_CAPITAL) and section (BS) match; only the scope differs, which is exactly what the acknowledgement records.
declarations.wi3ScopeNuance: the sentence speaks of 'the Company' (parent). It is applied to the consolidated block because consolidated owners' equity comprises only equity share capital (₹2,071 crore) and other equity (₹86,045 crore), with non-controlling interests (₹345 crore) separately presented, and no preference instrument appears in the consolidated balance sheet or in the authorised share capital (480,00,00,000 equity shares of ₹5 each only).

finding: All four mappings are internally consistent with the closed tables and are accepted. The one cross-scope mapping (PREFERENCE_CAPITAL) is the case the new grammar forces into the data as acceptedBy=… rather than leaving it in prose.
whatWouldHaveBeenRefused: A nil borrowing quoting a trade-payables sentence declared as class=TRADE_BALANCES, a balance-sheet item declared as PNL evidence, an unbound declaration under schema V3, and the preference-capital sentence offered for a consolidated row without an acknowledgement.
